contenders.handicapper_notes: Patrick Payne 4yo mare who ran a tremendous 2nd over 1100m on this Wangaratta surface on October 26, beaten only a half-length after driving hard late into the uphill 350m straight. Draws the golden inside marble in barrier 3, perfectly positioned to take cover down the 1000m-to-600m descent and unleash off the home bend. Billy Egan retains the ride with strong stable strike rates (22%). Clearly the runner to beat under set weights.

Consistent Cranbourne-trained mare with 5 placings from 7 starts. Hit the line solidly for 2nd at St Arnaud over 1100m last start and brings proven tactical versatility. Stalking run style (P) suits the Wangaratta 1170m sprint start, though barrier 7 forces Jake Noonan to slot in for cover before the downhill dip. Serious podium threat.

Local Ben Brisbourne runner entering peak 3rd-up fitness (+1.5 pts) with home track familiarity. Produced solid on-pace efforts at Echuca in both runs this preparation, including a close 3rd over 1200m on November 3. Lachlan King maps into a prominent one-off stalking position from barrier 6. Genuine contender right in the finish.

Key danger horse of the race. Flew home from last on the turn to finish 4th, beaten just 1.3 lengths behind Super Scholar and Kinky Mistress over 1100m here on October 26. Draws barrier 2 today, allowing Ryan Hurdle to save ground before utilizing the inside cutaway rail on the uphill 350m home straight. Lethal late turn-of-foot.

McEvoy-trained 3yo filly by Tagaloa carrying a light 56kg. Finished 6th beaten 3.2 lengths in the same track reference race behind Super Scholar and Kinky Mistress, where she peaked on her run after turning 3rd. Strips much fitter second-up and barrier 4 provides a soft midfield run behind the speed. Must be included in exotics.

Freedman-trained 3yo gelding gaining a start following scratchings. Struggled from a wide gate here first-up over 1100m on soft ground behind I Am Da Boss, but possesses sharp Cranbourne trial form. Will need luck from the wide barrier but will appreciate the drier Good 4 deck.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Top selection. Prepared by Lindsay Park Euroa stable (Ben, Will & JD Hayes) which historically excels at Wangaratta (+3.0 venue bonus). Resumes from a spell after showing strong provincial form when a close second over 1400m at Bendigo. Tripped stylishly to win an 1000m Pakenham trial on Nov 4 under a hold. Maps to box-seat or stalk the speed from barrier 4, preserving energy down the 1000m-600m downhill chute before using her stamina up the testing 350m straight.

Key danger. Delivered an eye-catching effort here over 1300m on Oct 26 when closing stoutly for 4th behind Princess Geisha, clocking the quickest final furlong of the race. Gets barrier 2 with Jake Noonan retaining the ride, guaranteeing an economical low-drag rail trail before the cutaway straight. The extra 100m to 1400m is ideal.

Flagged as the primary danger horse. Proven distance specialist at 1400m with two runner-up finishes, including a nose second at Seymour BM30k. Resumed over an inadequate 1100m sprint here and now steps up second-up to her pet trip. Slides inward considerably following five scratchings, and Brittany Button claim provides effective weight relief.

Representing the Mark Walker Cranbourne stable. Over-raced when stepped up to 1860m at Avoca last start after pressing the pace. Sharply dropping back to 1400m where her early speed can be better controlled by Jett Stanley. If she handles the downhill tempo shift smoothly, she will be in the firing line turning for home.

Second runner from the Hayes stable with Damien Thornton booked. Showed metro-provincial potential at 2 when 4th at Bendigo. Needed the run first-up over 1100m on soft ground at Kilmore and will appreciate stepping out to 1400m on a firmer Good 4 surface.

Foxwedge debutante for Vincent Malady drawn favorably in barrier 3. Fitted with blinkers for race debut following a recent Mortlake jump-out over 1300m where she stayed on nicely. Apprentice Sarah Field takes the ride from an inside lane.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Dominant top selection dropping sharply in class from the Listed Hill Smith Stakes (1800m) at Morphettville Parks into a North-East Victorian regional BM56. Scored an impressive 1600m maiden victory two back at Tatura registering a meeting-best 70 speed rating, and previously showed sharp aptitude when fourth beaten only 0.8L over 1400m here at Wangaratta. Maps perfectly from barrier 5 under Brad Rawiller to stalk midpack before utilizing Wangaratta's sweeping cambered bend and launching a sustained surge up the 3.0m uphill home straight.

Primary danger peaking third-up. Responded with a determined run to miss by a nose in a 1600m Class 1 at Wagga carrying 59kg on October 30. Proven winner at the mile with solid closing splits, well-suited to the genuine tempo generated by contested speed down the 1000m-600m downhill slope. Cory Parish retains the ride for Craig Widdison and should have this gelding winding up strongly out wide in the straight.

Cranbourne visitor from the Mark Walker stable boasting strong Benchmark 56 credentials. Won at Wodonga three back and produced a solid fifth beaten under two lengths over 1400m at Echuca on October 19. Gains significant tactical advantage from barrier 3, positioned to track leaders along the inside rail and capitalize on any cutaway sprint lanes in the home straight with Liana Wood in the saddle.

Local contender from the Ledger yard who thrives at this circuit, having placed over this track and distance in BM0-56 company in May. Won smartly at Wodonga over 1400m two back and held ground for third in a 1600m highweight at Echuca on November 3. Although drawn awkwardly in barrier 13, Blaike McDougall picks up the mount and brings top-tier local race craft to negotiate a stalking position.

Finished an encouraging fourth over this exact course and distance in BM56 company on October 26, beaten 3.6 lengths behind Positivo after making up ground from the rear. Won over this track and distance previously. Fourth-up now and reaches peak conditioning to hit the line stoutly up the uphill straight under Dylan Dunn.

Tough country mare entering off a gritty victory over 1600m in BM50 grade at Tumut. Raced prominently throughout and gets valuable weight relief down to 56.5kg with Cassidy Hill claiming 2kg. Will look to race on the pace, though facing pressure from drawn-wide speed rivals could test her reserves climbing the final 350m uphill gradient.

Maps to settle midfield with cover down Wangaratta's 1000m-600m descent before launching up the 350m uphill straight with a manageable 59.5kg under Standard pace.

Proven course-and-distance winner (P) who tracked the speed (2-2-2-1) and scored by 2.3L over this 2000m circuit on Good 4 ground 21 days ago (SR 58). Carries 59.0kg and slides to barrier 10 after scratches; the 2000m chute gives her ample run-up to slot into a forward stalking spot behind the two leaders.

Progressive 3yo filly with early speed (E) who dominated an 1800m Wycheproof maiden by 3.8L second-up (SR 61). Third-up peak fitness stepping to 2000m, slides into barrier 6, and gets apprentice weight relief via Nadia Daniels off 59.0kg. With Dance Lady also showing speed, it is a Standard pace map rather than Lone Speed, so she must rate kindly down the hill.

Class Drop Bonus applied: drops from Tier 2 Provincial Mornington BM66 (beaten 3.6L with a field-best recent SR 65 within 15 days) into Tier 2.5 Country BM56. Swooper (S) who won his Echuca 2100m maiden prior and slides to barrier 3 to conserve energy. Heavy 61.5kg on Wangaratta's 3.0m uphill straight slightly tempers his upside.

Danger Horse on his home track for Ben Brisbourne. Tactical presser (P) drawn barrier 2 with the portable rail Out 4m, setting up a golden box-seat and cutaway-rail trip behind the pace. Consistent at 2000m (5th here last start SR 59, 2nd at Wodonga prior) and carries 60.0kg.

Second-up improver (P) coming off a strong 1600m Mortlake maiden win on Soft ground (SR 54). Drawn barrier 1 for an economical inside trail with the rail Out 4m, though he faces a sharp distance jump from 1600m to 2000m while carrying 61.5kg up the testing straight.
